conventions.convention: For Hermitian M with M²=I, outcome b uses P_b=(I+(-1)^b M)/2 and probability Tr(ρP_b). The conditional state is P_bρP_b/p_b only for p_b>0; a zero-probability branch receives ⊥, meaning no assigned conditional density operator. At n=0 the admitted observables are ±I on C.
A stabilizer subgroup is abelian, consists of Hermitian Pauli operators, and excludes -I. Its rank is the binary dimension of its label span.

Rows store exact operators P(k,x,z)=i^k X^x Z^z, with k modulo four, coordinate order (x,z), and Hermiticity criterion k≡x·z modulo two. A generator tableau stores n commuting Hermitian rows with independent labels and excludes -I; destabilizers are optional.
The pure stabilizer state is a ray in the common +1 fixed space of a rank-n subgroup; a normalized vector is only a representative.
Adaptive control is a finite rooted tree. Gate nodes have one successor; measurement edges are labelled 0 and 1. Zero-weight edges have no conditional state and their descendants are not evaluated.
Circuit wires j=0,…,n-1 correspond to Pauli wires a=j+1. The simulator stores generator rows only and uses fresh fair bits exactly for anticommuting measurement cases.

load_bearing.statement: For a stabilizer subgroup S on n≥0 qubits, the label restriction is injective, its image L is an isotropic F₂-subspace, its dimension depends only on S, and |S|=2^dim L.
If L≤F₂^(2n) is isotropic with r=dim L under the standard symplectic form, then dim L⊥=2n-r. Consequently r≤n, and if r=n then L⊥=L.
For a stabilizer subgroup S, Π_S=|S|⁻¹∑g∈S g is self-adjoint and idempotent, with image exactly the common +1 fixed space. If this image is spanned by a unit vector ψ, then Π_S=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|.
For a rank-r stabilizer subgroup S on n qubits, Tr(Π_S)=dim_C im Π_S=2^n/|S|=2^(n-r). In particular, rank n gives a one-dimensional common fixed space.

For a density operator ρ and Hermitian Pauli M with M²=I on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, P_b=(I+(-1)^b M)/2 are complementary orthogonal projections, and p_b=Tr(ρP_b) satisfy p_b≥0 and p_0+p_1=1.

For n independent stabilizer generators fixing a unit vector ψ, if Hermitian M anticommutes with g₁, replace g₁ by (-1)^b M and each other anticommuting g_j by g_jg₁. For either outcome b, the updated rows generate a rank-n stabilizer subgroup for P_bψ/‖P_bψ‖.

For a rank-n stabilizer tableau and Hermitian Pauli measurement M, the tableau rule gives exactly the projective instrument branches: anticommuting cases have two probability-1/2 outcomes with the pivot-update conditional states; commuting cases give the unique probability-one signed outcome, unchanged state, and no normalized state for the opposite branch.

For finite adaptive H,S,S†,CNOT and Hermitian-Pauli circuits on n≥0 ordered qubits from computational-basis input, the generator-tableau simulator samples exactly the transcript and final-ray distribution. With T quantum instructions and C_cl controller bit operations per branch, time is O((n+1)²+T(n+1)³+C_cl), tableau/elimination workspace is O((n+1)²), and transcript storage is O(T).

|L|=2^r, including r=0.

seams_checked.note: Ordered wires, chronological unitary action, and separate classical resource charges are preserved. The adaptive measurement tree is defined locally rather than attributed to unitary circuit syntax.
Dirac expressions respect the root inner product linear in its first argument. Pure branch probabilities use the stated projection-norm identity.

Projective measurements permit zero projections. The local proof establishes complete positivity for every finite ancilla and trace preservation for every operator, matching the instrument definition; zero-weight conditional states remain undefined.

Exact modulo-four phases, X-before-Z multiplication, binary symplectic commutation, and Hermitian phase parity are preserved. H, S, inverse-S, and CNOT updates agree with these conventions; n=0 is supplied separately.
Density operators have nonzero finite-dimensional domains and trace one. Stabilizer states are rays, with unit representatives used only through their well-defined rank-one density projectors.
The displayed X,Y,Z,H,S matrices and Y=iXZ convention match the measurement example and phase-aware gate updates.
Tensor order, computational-basis normalization, big-endian encoding, and the empty tensor register C are preserved. The circuit-to-Pauli wire-index conversion is explicit.
The code projector theorem uses the same independent-label rank and exclusion of -I. The logical quotient theorem uses the isotropic label image and code dimension within their stated n≥1 domain.

The unique-ray theorem establishes a normalized graph state, independent commuting generators, and exclusion of -I before applying the average-projector and rank formulas. Its empty-graph case agrees with the one-dimensional empty register.
